the תנא at 31b.7: begins with the verse before, ends with the verse after
ואיתימא ריש לקיש (31b.10) -- the variant attribution of the תכלה שנה reason
the mishnah (Rosh Hashana 16a) cited דתנן at 31b.11: ובעצרת על פירות האילן
דאפכי להו (32a.1, 32a.5) -- the tradition that reverses R' Meir's and R' Yehuda's names
R' Yannai son of R' Yannai the Elder; transmits in R' Yannai Rabba's name (32a.16)

props.gloss_en: and one does not break off in [the reading of] the curses
Reish Lakish: [one does not break off in the curses] because one does not say a blessing over calamity
the baraita: when he begins, he begins with the verse before them; when he ends, he ends with the verse after them
they taught [ein mafsikin] only of the curses in Torat Kohanim (Leviticus)
but in the curses in Mishne Torah (Deuteronomy) he may break off
these [Leviticus] are stated in the plural, and Moshe said them from the mouth of the Almighty
and these [Deuteronomy] are stated in the singular, and Moshe said them himself
Levi bar Buti was reading and stammering before Rav Huna in the ארורי; Rav Huna said to him: as you wish [you may stop]
Ezra enacted for Israel that they read the curses of Torat Kohanim before Atzeret
and those of Mishne Torah before Rosh Hashana
so that the year may end together with its curses
yes -- Atzeret too is a new year
the mishnah: and on Atzeret [the world is judged] for the fruit of the tree
if elders tell you 'demolish' and children 'build', demolish and do not build, for the demolishing of elders is building and the building of youths is demolishing
and the sign of the matter: Rechavam son of Shlomo
where they stop on Shabbat morning, there they read at mincha (both tannaim)
R' Meir: where they stop at mincha, there they read on Monday; where on Monday, there on Thursday; where on Thursday, there on the coming Shabbat
R' Yehuda: where they stop on Shabbat morning, there they read at mincha, on Monday, on Thursday and on the coming Shabbat
R' Zeira's wording: the halakha is -- where they stop on Shabbat morning, there they read at mincha, on Monday, on Thursday and on the coming Shabbat
R' Meir: he opens and looks, rolls [it closed] and blesses, and opens again and reads
R' Yehuda: he opens and looks and blesses and reads
Ulla: why did they say the Torah reader should not assist the translator? so that people should not say the translation is written in the Torah
here too [R' Meir's reason]: so that people should not say the blessings are written in the Torah
and R' Yehuda: with the translation one may err; with the blessings one will not err
Rav Matna's wording: the halakha is -- he opens and looks and blesses and reads
the luchot and the bimot have nothing of sanctity in them
one who rolls a Torah scroll must set it [closed] at the seam
one who rolls a Torah scroll rolls it from the outside and not from the inside
and when he tightens it, he tightens it from the inside and not from the outside
of ten who read in the Torah, the greatest among them rolls the Torah scroll
the one who rolls it takes the reward of all of them
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: of ten who read in the Torah, the one who rolls the scroll received the reward of all of them
rather say: he received a reward equal to [that of] all of them
one may make use of a bat kol
as it is said: 'and your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying' (Isa 30:21)
and this is when he heard a man's voice in the town or a woman's voice in the field
and that is when it said 'yes, yes', or when it said 'no, no'
whoever reads [Torah] without melody and studies without song -- of him the verse says 'and I also gave them statutes that were not good...' (Ezek 20:25)

Rav Mesharshiya: two Torah scholars who dwell in one town and are not pleasant to one another in halakha -- of them the verse says 'statutes that were not good, and judgments by which they shall not live'
whoever holds a Torah scroll bare is buried bare
rather say: he is buried bare of mitzvot
Abaye: he is buried bare of that mitzva
better that the wrapper be rolled [around the scroll] and the Torah scroll not be rolled
